acceptance.output_evidence: THE SECOND CONTROL IDENTIFIED AND ITS PARAMETERS READ, NOT RECALLED. The rule holding the login path is AuthLoginRateLimit, Priority 2, Action Block, on opal-cloudfront-protection (6 rules total: BlockedIPs p0, RateLimitRule p1 Limit 2000, AuthLoginRateLimit p2, then three managed groups at Count p3-5). READ PARAMETERS: RateBasedStatement Limit=100, EvaluationWindowSec=300, AggregateKeyType=IP. SCOPE, decoded from the rule's own OrStatement ByteMatch SearchStrings (UriPath, STARTS_WITH, LOWERCASE): 'L2F1dGgvbG9naW4='='/auth/login', 'L2F1dGgvZm9yZ290LXBhc3N3b3Jk'='/auth/forgot-password', 'L2F1dGgvcmVzZXQtcGFzc3dvcmQ='='/auth/reset-password'. DOES ITS SCOPE COVER THE THROTTLE'S REQUESTS: YES and it is exact. The throttle guards login (LOGIN_THROTTLE, at /auth/login via index.ts:198) and reset (RESET_THROTTLE, at /auth/reset-password and reached from /auth/forgot-password), and all three of those paths are in the rule's scope-down. LIVE ASSOCIATION verified on the APPLIED plane, because a rule that exists but is not attached protects nothing: get-distribution EVTSA9VEHNZVH (Status Deployed, aliases opalinvest.dev + www.opalinvest.dev) reads WebACLId = arn:aws:wafv2:us-east-1:313476888478:global/webacl/opal-cloudfront-protection/a09833c0-4043-49fc-a92c-0dcdeaff9abd -- the same ACL -- and the live behavior /auth/* -> APIGateway-portal is 1 of 27 cache behaviors on that distribution. 'It exists' is not the criterion; 'it covers these requests at this threshold' is, and both are read. ONE COVERAGE GAP NAMED, not a defect of this face: the ENROLL_THROTTLE path /auth/mfa/enroll/send-code (index.ts:299) is NOT in the WAF rule's scope-down -- but its own design (throttle.ts:59-65) is account-keyed and its abuse bound is a texting budget, not a login-guess rate, so it is out of FWD-7's scope; recorded so a later reader does not mistake the WAF's three-path scope for total /auth/ coverage.
acceptance.denominator: 1 rule of 6 on the ACL identified as the login-path control; 3 of 3 scope-down paths decoded and matched against the throttle's guarded paths; 1 of 1 live WebACL association on the serving distribution; 27 cache behaviors of which /auth/* is 1.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: `S7-AC3` -- THE COVERAGE IS EXERCISED IN BOTH CONDITIONS AND THEY DIFFER: a burst with the throttle healthy (captured: what blocked, and which control blocked it) and a burst with the throttle's bookkeeping unavailable (captured: same). **The discriminator is that the second condition still blocks.** State the method used to create the second condition, its ledger entry and that it was reverted. **If the two conditions cannot be distinguished by the evidence, this files `UNCOMPUTABLE` with the reason** -- an undifferentiated pair proves nothing about the fail-open window.
acceptance.invocation: A login-abuse burst against https://opalinvest.dev/auth/login with a FABRICATED non-account email and a fixed junk password (never a credential, never a real human), run in two conditions. Condition 2 (throttle blind) was produced by a reversible, GetItem-only IAM deny on opalinvest-auth-lambda-role -- opened in ledger opsec-s7-throttle-failopen-coverage, applied, exercised, and REVERTED in the same window.
acceptance.output_evidence: THE DISCRIMINATING PAIR, same burst shape, differing ONLY in throttle availability, and the second condition STILL BLOCKS. CONDITION 1 -- THROTTLE HEALTHY (PHASE A, before any IAM change), 8 POSTs to /auth/login: #1-5 -> HTTP 401 {"error":"Invalid email or password"}; #6-8 -> HTTP 429 {"error":"Too many attempts. Please try again later."}. The 429 is the THROTTLE -- Lambda JSON via API Gateway -- firing at LOGIN_THROTTLE.threshold=5, and the WAF counter was ~8 so it cannot be the WAF. WHICH CONTROL BLOCKED: the account-keyed DynamoDB throttle. CONDITION 2 -- THROTTLE BLIND (PHASE C, GetItem deny in force, confirmed explicitDeny by simulate before the burst), 120 POSTs to /auth/login on one fabricated account: 120 x HTTP 401, ZERO 429 -- the identical burst that 429'd at #6 when healthy is NEVER blocked by the throttle, because enforceThrottle's GetItem is denied and the :112 path fails OPEN. Then PHASE C2 (still blind), 60 further POSTs after AWS WAF rate-aggregation caught up: 60 x HTTP 403 with server=CloudFront and an HTML edge body (NOT the Lambda's JSON) -- the WAF AuthLoginRateLimit blocking at its IP threshold WHILE the throttle is blind. WHICH CONTROL BLOCKED: the IP-keyed edge WAF. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS SATISFIED: condition 1's door is held by the throttle (429), condition 2's door -- with the throttle unable to read its table -- is held by the WAF (403); the two are distinguished by both status code and response source, and the second still blocks. NOTE ON WAF LATENCY, because it changed the probe shape: AWS WAF rate-based rules aggregate over a trailing window and engage the block with a lag, so the first 120-request blind burst completed at 401 before the block engaged; the follow-on 60-request burst, once the trailing count was aggregated above 100, returned 403 throughout. The lag is a property of the instrument, not evidence the WAF failed to cover the window.
acceptance.denominator: 2 conditions of 2 (throttle healthy, throttle blind); PHASE A 8 requests (5x401 + 3x429); PHASE C 120 requests (120x401, 0x429); PHASE C2 60 requests (60x403); 1 IAM deny applied and 1 reverted, both simulate-verified on the applied plane.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: `S7-AC4` -- THE VERDICT IS STATED AS A VERDICT: either **FWD-7 IS SERVED** by the measured coverage, with the reasoning and the numbers, or **A GAP EXISTS**, named precisely, with a row id, and explicitly NOT remediated in this face. **Both are PASS outcomes for this criterion; the FAIL is an unstated verdict or a silently-closed gap.**
acceptance.invocation: Synthesis of S7-AC1/AC2/AC3: the measured coverage of the login path during the throttle's fail-open window.
acceptance.output_evidence: THE VERDICT, STATED AS A VERDICT: FWD-7 IS SERVED. FWD-7's DONE WHEN is 'losing the login throttle's bookkeeping never opens the door wider.' MEASURED: when the throttle's bookkeeping is unavailable (the exact GetItem-fail condition that drives every fail-open site), the login path is still rate-limited by the WAF AuthLoginRateLimit at 100 requests / 300s / IP, which is LIVE-associated with the serving distribution, scoped to /auth/login (+ forgot/reset), and -- being evaluated at the edge BEFORE the request reaches the Lambda -- does NOT share the throttle's DynamoDB failure mode. That last point is the reasoning: the two controls have DISJOINT dependencies (the throttle needs DynamoDB, the WAF does not), so the throttle's bookkeeping failure cannot widen the WAF's door, which is precisely FWD-7's bar. The numbers: healthy door closes at 5 attempts/account (throttle); blind door closes at 100 requests/IP (WAF); the fail-open transition moves the binding limit from a per-account count to a per-IP rate, but it never removes a limit. THE ONE NAMED RESIDUAL, not remediated here: the WAF's per-IP aggregation limits an attacker to 100 login attempts per IP per 5 minutes but does not enforce a per-ACCOUNT bound during the fail-open window, so a distributed (many-IP) low-per-IP credential-stuffing run against one account is bounded by the throttle when healthy and only loosely by the WAF when blind. This is a narrower door than 'no limit', so it does not violate FWD-7's 'never wider' bar; it is recorded as the honest edge of the coverage rather than a gap that blocks the face. No remedy is invented in this face.
acceptance.denominator: 1 verdict of 1 (SERVED, with the disjoint-dependency reasoning and both threshold numbers); 1 named residual (distributed low-per-IP stuffing), not remediated, not a gap that fails FWD-7's 'never wider' bar.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: `S7-AC5` -- NOTHING WAS MADE FAIL-CLOSED AND NOTHING PERMANENT CHANGED: a diff census of `throttle.ts` against HEAD showing **0 changes to its fail-open behaviour**, and a census of any temporary change made for AC3 showing it is REVERTED, read on the APPLIED plane after the revert with a positive control. The login path is left exactly as found.
acceptance.invocation: git diff --stat HEAD -- throttle.ts; git status --porcelain over the auth-handler src tree; aws iam list-role-policies before/after; aws iam simulate-principal-policy after the revert with a positive control; and a functional post-revert burst.
acceptance.output_evidence: NOTHING MADE FAIL-CLOSED AND NOTHING PERMANENT CHANGED. throttle.ts: git diff --stat HEAD is EMPTY -- 0 changes to its fail-open behaviour; the file was READ, never edited. The whole auth-handler src tree: git status --porcelain is clean, no file touched. THE TEMPORARY CHANGE, made only to produce S7-AC3's second condition, IS REVERTED and the revert is read on the APPLIED plane with a positive control: list-role-policies before = [cross-firm-secret-deny, opalinvest-auth-permissions, PartnerIdentityReadPermissions, ses-send-email]; during = those four + s7-tmp-throttle-getitem-deny; after the delete-role-policy = the original four, s7-tmp absent. simulate-principal-policy after the revert: dynamodb:GetItem on the throttle table -> allowed (matched the original opalinvest-auth-permissions); POSITIVE CONTROL, a separate call, dynamodb:GetItem on a table the role does not hold -> implicitDeny, so the tool discriminates and the 'allowed' is a real allow. FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END CONFIRMATION (PHASE D), a fresh fabricated non-account, 8 POSTs after the revert: #1-5 -> 401, #6 -> 429 -- the throttle blocks at threshold 5 again, identical to PHASE A, so the GetItem revert restored the throttle behaviour end-to-end and not merely in the policy document. THE WAF RATE-STATE WAS TRANSIENT: a 3-request probe between the revert and PHASE D returned 401 (not 403), so the AuthLoginRateLimit rate-counter on the probe IP lapsed on its own; no standing block was left on the login path. The login path is left exactly as found.
acceptance.denominator: 1 source file (throttle.ts) diffed = 0 changes; auth-handler src tree = 0 files changed; role inline-policy set 4 before / 5 during / 4 after; 1 revert simulate-verified with 1 positive control; 1 functional 8-request re-confirmation (5x401 + 429 at #6).

mutant.description: The control that AC3 designates as the one that must be able to FAIL: if the login burst blocked IDENTICALLY whether or not the throttle could read its table, the evidence would not discriminate and the criterion would have to file UNCOMPUTABLE. The mutant is the throttle-blind condition itself -- a real GetItem deny applied to the live role -- run against the throttle-healthy baseline.
mutant.expected: If the throttle contributes nothing distinguishable, the blind burst blocks the same way the healthy burst does (429 at 6) or not at all. If it discriminates, the blind burst does NOT 429 (fail-open) and the block, when it comes, comes from a different control.
mutant.observed: DISCRIMINATED. Healthy: 429 at request 6 (throttle, Lambda JSON). Blind: 120 requests with ZERO 429 (the throttle demonstrably stopped blocking) and then 403 from CloudFront (a different control, the edge WAF). The pair is differentiated by status code AND response source, so AC3 is a PASS-SERVED and not an UNCOMPUTABLE. A SECOND, INDEPENDENT CONTROL rode the IAM verification: the simulate positive controls -- UpdateItem allowed while GetItem denied (deny is surgical), and GetItem on a non-held table returning implicitDeny after the revert (the allow is real) -- so the deny and its revert were each confirmed on the applied plane and not asserted.

determinism.method: The throttle-healthy 429-at-threshold-5 behaviour was observed twice on independent fabricated accounts: PHASE A (before any change) and PHASE D (after the revert), each 8 requests.
determinism.observed: STABLE. Both runs: 401 for requests 1-5, 429 from request 6, on LOGIN_THROTTLE.threshold=5. The blind condition's zero-429 result was likewise observed across 120 requests, not a single sample. The only non-repeated value was the WAF's block-engagement point, which AWS rate-aggregation makes non-deterministic in timing by design; the block's OCCURRENCE (403 from the edge while blind) is the stable fact, its exact request index is not, and the proof claims only the occurrence.

declared_exclusions.item: The IP-blindness of throttle.ts (throttle.ts:14 -- /auth/* forwards no CloudFront-* headers)
declared_exclusions.reason: Its CAUSE is upstream of this file, in the CloudFront /auth/* behavior's origin-request header forwarding, not in throttle.ts. The face names it (READ LIVE section) as 'a different surface from this one' and routes it to L4 as a candidate remedy for another lane. Read and used to explain WHY the throttle must be account-keyed (it cannot see the IP), not fixed here.

declared_exclusions.item: The ENROLL_THROTTLE path /auth/mfa/enroll/send-code, absent from the WAF rule's scope-down
declared_exclusions.reason: Out of FWD-7's scope. FWD-7 is about the LOGIN path's fail-open; the enrolment throttle guards a texting budget (throttle.ts:59-65), is account-keyed by deliberate design, and its abuse model is mail-amplification, not login-guessing. Recorded in S7-AC2 so the WAF's three-path scope is not mistaken for total /auth/ coverage; not a gap this face owns.

An explicit STOP per the face's first section and FWD-7's bar: a rate-limiter that takes down login on a DynamoDB blip converts a bookkeeping failure into an outage, which is a WIDER door than the one FWD-7 is about. Nothing in this face touches the fail-open behaviour; the whole deliverable is a measurement that the fail-open window is covered, not a change to it.

declared_exclusions.item: The WAF managed-rule-group and rate-limit configuration (TO-OP-S-4-18 / OP-s-4)
declared_exclusions.reason: Read-only dependency (OP-s-4). The ACL's rules were READ to identify and parameterise the second control; nothing was edited. The managed-group work belongs to TO-OP-S-4-18.

declared_exclusions.item: A remedy for the distributed low-per-IP credential-stuffing residual named in S7-AC4
declared_exclusions.reason: The face forbids inventing a remedy inside this measurement face (deliverable 3). The residual is a narrower door than 'no limit' and does not fail FWD-7's 'never wider' bar, so it is stated as the honest edge of the coverage; any remedy is a separate cut for L4/L5 to decide.
